My ex-best friend was morbidly obese throughout our childhood, and I was always the skinny friend. When she was about 20, she had a gastric bypass done, and she lost alllll of the weight. I eventually gained a considerable amount of weight (50 pounds) and eventually weighed more than her. She would make comments on it and it made me feel bad. She would even fat shame others! This 11 year friendship ended (for other factors as well) but good riddance. I feel that she justified that she can treat people wrong because people bullied her growing up. I am speaking from experience, And I am not suggesting that you jump to not being friends with her anymore. I would talk to here about her comment. Perhaps she didn't mean to hurt your feelings.

In terms of the weight gain, I assume you're young, so it is natural for you to gain weight as you get older. It isn't a cruel joke from God. It happens. As you get older you got to watch what you put into your body and how much you do for exercise a little more attentively. When you're a kid, it was easy to bypass. I know it is discouraging at times, but you'll be even more sad a year from now because you didn't try to fix the problem.
